main_body: A wooden pew bench drawn as horizontal plank bands (stacked slats) between two vertical side posts, seen straight from the front
top_band: none distinct: rows 1-3 mid-brown (L=121) are the same family as the rest of the planks, and rows 7-10 are a lighter plank band (L=157/117), with no clear horizontal seat surface above a front face
evidence: The column reads as alternating plank bands: dark line, 3 mid-brown rows, dark gap, light band, dark gap, mid band. Every band sits in the same lightness family, and the lighter rows 7 and 10 are thin lines with a dark row between them. No seat surface is seen from above. It is a flat front view of a backrest and slats, like the red front-elevation guide. The seat-kind requirement (seat surface seen from above) is not met.

style.evidence: Only 8 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 8 colours per tile against 17-20. The plank bands have almost no grain or dots, with only a few small speckles on the mid band. Outlines are brown-tinted and not neutral black (17% neutral), which is acceptable. Shading is a few stripe tones with no per-plank highlight or wood grain, so it reads as much thinner and flatter than the stall and well references.
